fact: NCRA says over 80% of integrated CRVS and ID services, including birth registration, are digitized and decentralized across regional and district offices.
system: NCRA integrated CRVS and ID services

fact: The Calabash Newspaper reports a one-year Vital Strategies-funded NCRA project integrating digital technologies into birth and death registration, with 48 laptops and modems for 48 health facilities in 16 districts.
system: Strengthening Births and Deaths Registration Services within the CRVS System in Sierra Leone

fact: UNICEF's 6 October 2026 story says the NCRA registered a baby's birth in Bombali District on a portable digital device through Sierra Leone's digital birth registration system, which NCRA's Bombali District Registration Officer calls an integral part of the civil registration system.

NCRA's Director-General says an integrated electronic CRVS system, digitising and consolidating civil registration, vital statistics and identity management on one modular platform, has been developed with government and EU support; no national in-service rollout or birth coverage is stated.
Sierra Leone's Amb. Mohamed Mubashir Massaquoi said fully electronic birth registration was launched in 2022.
Massaquoi said Sierra Leone's civil registration rose from about 7 percent a decade ago to 90 percent, a rate not stated to be of the digital system.
The World Bank's WDI lists completeness of birth registration in Sierra Leone at 90.4% for 2019, a national rate not tied to a digital system.
